notes: The supplied description and p. 3 locator identify the bi-factor replication broadly but do not specify a model contrast, goodness-of-fit test, factor, or item. All three assigned rows have identical target descriptions and locators. Section 3.2 reports several candidate tests; the rows cannot be assigned to them by order or numerical matching. Candidate paired tests, not assigned to any row: content-specific bi-factor versus content-specific model, Δχ2(12) = 206.24, p < .001; content-specific bi-factor versus valence bi-factor, Δχ2(4) = 50.16, p < .001; alternative valence bi-factor versus valence bi-factor, Δχ2(4) = 11.65, p = .020. These are printed chi-square difference tests, not converted effects. Table 1 additionally reports model goodness-of-fit chi-squares (including content-specific bi-factor χ2 = 518.83, df = 75), without model p values. Tables 2 and 3 contain item loadings and factor variance/reliability metrics, respectively; the input does not identify a particular item or factor. No candidate is promoted to the row-specific es or p fields. Candidate model N = 3906 participants, explicitly printed in Table 1, not inferred from df or a recruitment-only total. Participants are adolescents from 13 Netherlands high schools; 13 is a school count, not participant N. Section 3.1 reports 0.5 % missing data, and section 2.3 says missing data was handled through multiple imputation. No additional exclusions are specified in these sections. No N sum or arithmetic is used. Because the requested row-specific test remains unresolved, model N is retained only as a candidate for parent field-scope review. Reported success is the authors’ overall verdict on the described bi-factor replication; it does not resolve the row-specific contrast. Original fields are unassigned placeholders. Supplied primary PDF pages 2–4 were rendered and visually inspected; evidence quotes refer to canonical supplied text.
